title: Cohomology commutes with direct sums of modules on a qcqs scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in I}$ be any family of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$ be their direct sum, i.e. a coproduct in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with inclusions $\iota_i:\mathcal F_i\to\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$, and let $p\ge0$. The canonical $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}H^p(X,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(X,\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)$ from the direct sum of modules [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], whose restriction to the $i$-th summand is $H^p(X,\iota_i)$, is an isomorphism [pqf-def-cohomology]. In particular this holds for the family indexed by the nonnegative graded pieces of a quasi-coherent graded module.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01FF (lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit, lines 3194-3225), applied to the directed system of finite partial direct sums; its topological hypotheses hold for the underlying space of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. The finite sums commute with cohomology by additivity. Tag verified in tags/tags: 01FF,cohomology-lemma-quasi-separated-cohomology-colimit.

proof.text: (Hypotheses of 01FF.) Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its underlying topological space is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. By the definition of a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] the quasi-compact open subsets of $X$ form a basis of the topology and the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact; moreover $U=X$ is itself a quasi-compact open subset. So [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] applies to $X$ with $U=X$, and then $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=H^p(X,\mathcal G)$ is the cohomology of the statement.

source.place: Coherent, proof of Lemma 07TB (label lemma-colimit-cohomology, lines 1157-1164): 'the basis of affine opens ... satisfies the assumptions of that lemma'; Cohomology, Lemma 01FF hypotheses (1), (2) (lines 3196-3201)

proof.text: (The finite partial sums.) Write $\mathcal F=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$. The category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so it has finite biproducts [def-sp-abelian]: for every finite subset $J\subseteq I$ choose an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F_J$ with morphisms $\iota^J_j:\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal F_J$, $p^J_j:\mathcal F_J\to\mathcal F_j$ ($j\in J$) such that $p^J_k\iota^J_j=\mathrm{id}$ if $k=j$ and $=0$ if $k\neq j$, and $\sum_{j\in J}\iota^J_jp^J_j=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_J}$ ($\mathcal F_\emptyset=0$). Then $(\mathcal F_J,(\iota^J_j)_{j\in J})$ is a coproduct of $(\mathcal F_j)_{j\in J}$: given morphisms $g_j:\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal M$, the morphism $u=\sum_jg_jp^J_j$ satisfies $u\iota^J_k=g_k$, and any $u$ with $u\iota^J_k=g_k$ for all $k$ equals $u\sum_j\iota^J_jp^J_j=\sum_jg_jp^J_j$. For $J\subseteq J'$ finite let $\kappa_{J'J}:\mathcal F_J\to\mathcal F_{J'}$ be the morphism with $\kappa_{J'J}\iota^J_j=\iota^{J'}_j$, and $\kappa_J:\mathcal F_J\to\mathcal F$ the morphism with $\kappa_J\iota^J_j=\iota_j$ ($j\in J$). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-coproduct-finite-subsums] (2), applied to the family $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in I}$ with these coproducts for finite subsets and $(\mathcal F,(\iota_i))$ for $A'=I$, the finite subsets $J\subseteq I$ form a directed set, $(\mathcal F_J,\kappa_{J'J})$ is a system over it, and $(\mathcal F,(\kappa_J)_J)$ is its colimit in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. (Clause (1) of that node guarantees that the coproduct $\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$ of the statement exists.)

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 09J7 (label lemma-perfect-is-compact, lines 13758-13768): $H^p(X,\bigoplus_i\mathcal I_i)=\bigoplus_iH^p(X,\mathcal I_i)$ 'by Lemma 01FF', the direct sum being the directed colimit of its finite partial sums (written out by the agent)

proof.text: (Finite sums: additivity.) $H^p(X,-)$ is the $p$-th right derived functor of the left exact additive functor $\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], which has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]; by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] the right derived functors form a $\delta$-functor, whose components are additive functors by the definition of a $\delta$-functor [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor], [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Hence for every finite $J\subseteq I$ the map $\Psi_J:\bigoplus_{j\in J}H^p(X,\mathcal F_j)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F_J)$, $(y_j)_j\mapsto\sum_{j\in J}H^p(X,\iota^J_j)(y_j)$, is bijective: additivity gives $H^p(X,p^J_k)H^p(X,\iota^J_j)=H^p(X,p^J_k\iota^J_j)$, which is $\mathrm{id}$ for $k=j$ and $H^p(X,0)=0$ for $k\neq j$, and $\sum_jH^p(X,\iota^J_j)H^p(X,p^J_j)=H^p(X,\sum_j\iota^J_jp^J_j)=\mathrm{id}$. So every $w\in H^p(X,\mathcal F_J)$ equals $\Psi_J\big((H^p(X,p^J_j)(w))_j\big)$ (surjectivity), and if $\Psi_J((y_j))=0$ then applying $H^p(X,p^J_k)$ gives $y_k=0$ for each $k$ (injectivity).

source.place: Cohomology, Section 01EO (cohomology as right derived functors, the functors $H^p(X,-)$ being additive), used implicitly in the proof of Lemma 09J7 (lines 13762-13768) (written out by the agent)

proof.text: (The canonical map and its finite pieces.) By the description of the direct sum of modules [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], an element $z=(z_i)_{i\in I}$ of $\bigoplus_iH^p(X,\mathcal F_i)$ has finite support, and the canonical map of the statement is $\Phi(z)=\sum_iH^p(X,\iota_i)(z_i)$, a finite sum; it is $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear since each $H^p(X,\iota_i)$ is, so it is an isomorphism as soon as it is bijective. For a finite $J\subseteq I$ containing the support of $z$, write $z|_J=(z_j)_{j\in J}$. Since $\kappa_J\iota^J_j=\iota_j$ and $H^p(X,-)$ is a functor [pqf-def-cohomology], $\Phi(z)=H^p(X,\kappa_J)\big(\Psi_J(z|_J)\big)$; likewise, for finite $J\subseteq J'$, $\kappa_{J'J}\iota^J_j=\iota^{J'}_j$ gives $H^p(X,\kappa_{J'J})\big(\Psi_J(z|_J)\big)=\Psi_{J'}(z|_{J'})$, where $z|_{J'}$ is $z|_J$ extended by zero.

source.place: Cohomology, proof of Lemma 09J7 (lines 13762-13768) (written out by the agent)

proof.text: (Surjectivity.) Let $x\in H^p(X,\mathcal F)$. By step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] (a) applied with $U=X$, $q=p$ to the directed system $(\mathcal F_J,\kappa_{J'J})$ with colimit $(\mathcal F,(\kappa_J))$ of step 2 gives a finite $J\subseteq I$ and $w\in H^p(X,\mathcal F_J)$ with $x=H^p(X,\kappa_J)(w)$. By step 3, $w=\Psi_J((y_j)_{j\in J})$ for some $y_j\in H^p(X,\mathcal F_j)$; let $z\in\bigoplus_iH^p(X,\mathcal F_i)$ be $(y_j)$ extended by zero. By step 4, $\Phi(z)=H^p(X,\kappa_J)(\Psi_J(z|_J))=x$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01FF (lines 3203-3209), applied as in the proof of Lemma 09J7 (lines 13762-13768)

proof.text: (Injectivity.) Let $z\in\bigoplus_iH^p(X,\mathcal F_i)$ with $\Phi(z)=0$, and let $J$ be a finite subset containing its support. By step 4, $w=\Psi_J(z|_J)\in H^p(X,\mathcal F_J)$ satisfies $H^p(X,\kappa_J)(w)=\Phi(z)=0$. By step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] (b) applied with $U=X$, $q=p$ to the system of step 2 gives a finite $J'\supseteq J$ with $H^p(X,\kappa_{J'J})(w)=0$. By step 4 this element is $\Psi_{J'}(z|_{J'})$, and $\Psi_{J'}$ is injective by step 3, so $z|_{J'}=0$; since the support of $z$ lies in $J\subseteq J'$, $z=0$. With step 5, $\Phi$ is a bijective $\mathcal O_X(X)$-linear map, hence an isomorphism.

proof.text: (The graded case.) For a quasi-coherent graded module $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}\mathcal G_m$ the statement is the case $I=\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$, $\mathcal F_m=\mathcal G_m$ of what was proved: nothing beyond the general case is used.
